rows.verified: COMAH 2015 applies to establishments holding dangerous substances at or above specified thresholds and replaced COMAH 1999 on 1 June 2015.
COMAH requires businesses to take necessary measures to prevent major accidents and limit consequences to people and the environment.
The regulatory aim treats serious harm to the environment as well as harm to people within major-accident control.
Operator duties are divided between lower-tier and upper-tier establishments according to dangerous-substance thresholds.
Every COMAH operator must prepare and retain a Major Accident Prevention Policy.
The safety-management system addresses organisation, hazard identification, operational control, management of change, emergency planning, monitoring, audit and review.
Upper-tier operators must prepare a safety report demonstrating arrangements to control major-accident hazards and limit consequences.
A safety report describes the establishment and surroundings, including geographical, meteorological, geological and hydrographic conditions.
The upper-tier safety report includes dangerous-substance classification and inventory information.
Safety reports describe possible major-accident scenarios, triggering conditions and internal or external causes.
Domino-group establishments must cooperate and share relevant information with neighbouring sites where interactions can increase risk or consequences.
Upper-tier operators must maintain a written internal emergency plan covering reasonably foreseeable low-probability, high-consequence events.
Operators supply information needed by local authorities to prepare external emergency plans for off-site consequences.
COMAH requires hazard and establishment information to be made publicly available through the Competent Authority.
Category 1 responders have a cooperation role in tests of upper-tier external emergency plans.
Safety reports must be reviewed when modifications or new information affect risk and at least every five years.
The COMAH Competent Authority assesses safety reports using high-level principles, assessment criteria and detailed technical guidance.
The public establishment register is operational information that can change as sites enter, leave or change tier.
Presence near a COMAH establishment identifies regulatory context but does not by itself quantify an individual parcel's accident probability.
A safety report documents controls and scenarios but is not evidence of current real-time plant condition or zero residual risk.
